Best regards,
Amir

devtools::install_github("Vitek-Lab/MSstats", ref = "hotfix-fractions-check"), this may solve the problem.

Kind regards,
Mateusz

Hi  Mateusz,

Just to update you, I have put together a tiny script to convert my data to the MSstats format and it went well. However, I found a significant difference between the output of the MSstats convertor function and mine. It seems that the approach is quite different. What the MSstats convertor does is to remove all transitions (fragment iones) with TRUE flag under F.ExcludedFromQuantification column (keep basically top3 FI based on SP suggestion). and then look at the qvalue on both protein and EG level. If the qvalue doesn't meet the threshold, the intensity would be replaced by 0 or NA. This looks to me a bit problematic. Because down the road, if we don't impute for missing values, those zeros are getting involved in (relative) quantification. So we are litterally involving less confident features (qvalue > threshold) with zeros value. Could you please review the approach behind the functions again? What I perefer and used always for my analysis (from several years ago when I processed my data by OpenSWATH) is to keep more fragment ions in and ignore those that didnt pass qvalue cutoff. even if you want to only keep top3 fragment ions based on SP suggestion, we should not replace the intensity of low confident one with zero keep them in. That would challenge the whole analysis particarly computed fold change. Please let me know how you think.

Best,
Amir
